chapter: New York bands and the first records
title: Syracuse Hotel job and hiring Hank D'Amico
summary: The band plays the Syracuse Hotel with singer Nancy Flake; Norvo hires clarinetist Hank D'Amico in Utica and gets NBC air time.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So now they got me a job at the Syracuse Hotel. So we had -- added a little girl singer, Nancy Flake. And the boys -- we didn't keep the boy, we kept the girl. So, Slats Long -- his wife worked the Roxie, so he wanted to stay in town, so he said he'd go up till I found somebody. Now we opened, we were a big hit in Syracuse, it was a wonderful thing. Was a great room and the band sounded good, it was soft --
And so one weekend, we had to work five days there, and I went over to Utica, and heard a kid in a d'Amico club, and I immediately hired him. It was Hank Damico.
So he came and joined us.

And then we did a few air shows out of there. Remember one that were on at NBC, and somebody in Chicago heard it and told them about it in Chicago. Don Roth came in from Chicago, and hired us for the Blackhawk.
